title: scicode-lint: Detecting Methodology Bugs in Scientific Python Code with LLM-Generated Patterns
analyses: code (LLM answers per-pattern yes/no questions at run time; patterns written by frontier LLMs at build time)
leak_types: scaler/preprocessing (ml-001, ml-007); target (ml-002); target encoding (ml-003); shuffled CV on temporal data (ml-005); forward shift / centered rolling (ml-006); train/test from same source without disjoint split, e.g. two .sample() calls (ml-009); multi-test (ml-010)
group_leakage: no (no pattern found in 66 pattern definitions)
temporal_leakage: yes, from code: ml-005 (shuffle=True in CV splitter or cross_val_score with explicit temporal evidence; shuffle=False and train_test_split not covered) and ml-006 (negative shift, center=True, future slicing)
verified_how: arXiv abstract + HTML read; PyPI 0.5.0 wheel pattern.toml files for ml-005/ml-006 read; grep of all pattern definitions, 2026-09-29
notes: Found in the Phase 1 boundary novelty search. Invalidates the claim that no code-level tool detects temporal leakage; adopted as the temporal baseline (decision 2026-09-29). Runtime needs a local 8B LLM (Qwen3-8B via vLLM on GPU in the paper). Paper reports 65% precision at 100% recall on Kaggle notebooks (preprocessing leakage, human labels); per-category holdout precision from the HTML summary (AI training 11%) not yet checked against the paper's table.
